raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

srt binds every scheduler process to its GPU's NUMA node by default (`SGLANG_AUTO_NUMA_BIND`, `numa_utils`). sglang-diffusion GPU workers were never bound. On a two-socket host, an unbound worker drifts to the other socket while its first-touch host memory stays behind, so every host-bound op pays remote-memory latency. The same configuration then lands in one of two modes from one run to the next.

GB300 (2x Grace; GPU0/1 on node 0, GPU2/3 on node 1), FLUX.1-dev TP2 eager with no other changes: 6.54, 4.30, 6.14, 6.49 s across runs. With the workers bound, it stays at about 4.0 s.

## Modifications

- `run_scheduler_process` binds the worker to its GPU's NUMA node before CUDA init and model load, so first-touch memory lands on the local node. It reuses srt's `get_numa_node_if_available` and `numa_bind_to_node` (in-process `sched_setaffinity` + preferred memory policy), so detection, `SGLANG_AUTO_NUMA_BIND=0`, permission checks and the failure semantics all match srt.
- srt's spawn-time `numactl` path (`configure_subprocess`) is not reused. `_mp_set_executable` asserts that the **global** multiprocessing start method is spawn, while diffusion launches workers from a local `mp.get_context("spawn")`, so the global method is still `fork` on Linux.
- New `--numa-node N [N ...]` with srt's meaning (the i-th value is for the worker on local GPU i), validated against the local worker count, plus a line in `api/cli.mdx`.

## Accuracy Tests

No numerical change: only CPU affinity and the host memory policy of the worker process change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

GB300, `sglang serve`, `/v1/images/generations`. Each value is the median of 5 requests after 2 warmups, with a fresh server per arm because placement is decided at startup. Arms are interleaved.

| Case | Unbound (main) | Bound |
|---|---|---|
| Cosmos3-Nano T2I 1280x720, 35 steps, CFG-parallel 2 GPUs, eager | 1.349 / 1.270 s | **0.919 / 0.967 s** (this PR, no numactl) |
| same, on GPUs 2,3 | – | 0.947 s; log: `GPU 0/1 worker bound to NUMA node 1` |
| FLUX.1-dev 1024², 50 steps, TP2, eager | 6.44 / 6.37 / 6.06 s | 3.98 / 4.00 / 3.83 s (`numactl` on node 0 as a stand-in) |

Why it matters there: per-rank torch-profiler traces of the unbound FLUX TP2 run show both ranks' main threads ~100% busy on the CPU side. Rank 1 GPU is 27% busy with 639 ms of gaps per 4 steps, while rank 0 spends 1.3 ms per custom all-reduce waiting for it. The step time is the slower rank's host time, so placement shows up 1:1 in latency.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests: `test_gpu_worker_cpu_threads.py` (explicit node indexed by local GPU, auto-detection queries the worker's own GPU, `SGLANG_AUTO_NUMA_BIND=0` leaves the worker unbound) and `test_server_args.py` (`--numa-node` parsing, length validation). Both files pass on GB300 (236 passed).
- [x] Update documentation (`docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/api/cli.mdx`).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

@@ -88,6 +88,7 @@ Use `sglang generate --help` and `sglang serve --help` for the full argument lis
 - PEFT `adapter_config.json` semantics are applied automatically for named adapter slots, RSLoRA, and per-layer `alpha_pattern`. Adapters that require unsupported auxiliary parameters or runtime behavior, such as DoRA, fail before weight injection instead of silently using ordinary LoRA math.
 - `--lora-merge-mode {auto|merge|dynamic}`: choose how LoRA is applied. `auto` statically merges regular weights and uses dynamic LoRA for FSDP-sharded weights to avoid full-gather peaks.
 - `--num-gpus {N}`: number of GPUs to use
+- `--numa-node {N} [N ...]`: NUMA node for each GPU worker, the i-th value for the worker on local GPU i. When unset, each worker binds its CPUs and host memory to its GPU's NUMA node on multi-socket hosts, as srt does; set `SGLANG_AUTO_NUMA_BIND=0` to turn that off. Unbound workers on a two-socket host (e.g. GB200/GB300) can drift to the other socket, which slows host-bound steps and makes latency vary run to run.
 - `--performance-mode {manual|auto|speed|memory}` / `--mode`: preset for latency/throughput and memory defaults. `auto` is the default and dispatches residency from selected-GPU headroom and workload type: image DiTs stay resident above the 45 GiB threshold, while video DiT placement remains model-specific. It uses FSDP only for validated DiT-offload replacement paths. `speed` keeps `torch.compile` disabled unless a model-specific deployment config opts in after validation; pass `--enable-torch-compile true` to enable it explicitly. Use `manual` to keep performance-related server args under explicit user control. Explicit offload, FSDP, and parallelism flags take precedence in all modes.
 - `--direct-gpu-weight-loading {true|false}`: opt into direct GPU loading for an unquantized, GPU-resident, TP=1 DiT by materializing its complete checkpoint state dict on GPU. Compatible tensors become parameter storage without another GPU copy, while tensors requiring transforms can still need temporary allocations. It is disabled by default; startup time and peak GPU memory remain model-dependent, so benchmark the target model before deployment. It is incompatible with DiT CPU/layerwise offload and FSDP.
 - `--tp-size {N}`: tensor parallelism size. Depending on the pipeline, it can shard the DiT, one or more encoders, or both.

+def _bind_worker_to_gpu_numa_node(
+    server_args: ServerArgs, local_rank: int

+    """Bind this worker's CPUs and host memory to its GPU's NUMA node, as srt does.

+    on that node; an unbound worker drifts across sockets and every

+        numa_bind_to_node,
+    )
+
+    numa_node = get_numa_node_if_available(server_args, local_rank)
+    if numa_node is not None:
+        numa_bind_to_node(numa_node)
+        logger.info("GPU %d worker bound to NUMA node %d", local_rank, numa_node)
+    return numa_node
+
